details: @langitdeveloper/baileys@2.1.0 is a republished fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library that silently manipulates the WhatsApp account it is connected with. On construction of the socket, lib/Socket/newsletter.js (makeNewsletterSocket, called from lib/Socket/messages-send.js for every message-sending socket) immediately downloads a remote list of WhatsApp channel IDs from hxxps://raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/FadelSM/IDCH/refs/heads/main/idch[.]json and, 90 seconds later, issues a FOLLOWER/subscribe GraphQL query (QueryIds.FOLLOW) for every JID in that list using the victim's authenticated session. The subscription set is controlled entirely by the third-party file, not by the caller, and an earlier ID-decoding step was removed from the code so the downloaded values are used verbatim. Separately, lib/Socket/dugong.js hardcodes the channel 120363430179804706@newsletter (display name "shenvn.") and attaches it as forwardedNewsletterMessageInfo context to messages generated through the library, attributing outgoing messages to that channel. The package.json preinstall hook only performs a Node version check. The package claims the name and scope of the upstream Baileys library but publishes under an unrelated scope, and its only external payload source is a GitHub repository unrelated to the claimed project. No npm/GitHub token,.npmrc, or environment-value access was found. A fork of the Baileys WhatsApp client published under an unofficial scope (`@langitdeveloper/baileys`) that silently enrols the authenticated user's WhatsApp account into third-party channels. In `lib/Socket/newsletter.js`, `makeNewsletterSocket()` starts an async task when the socket is created that fetches a channel list over HTTPS from `hxxps://raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/FadelSM/IDCH/refs/heads/main/idch[.]json`, then, after a 90-second `setTimeout`, issues the WhatsApp `w:mex` newsletter FOLLOW mutation (query id 7871414976211147) for every JID in that list via `Promise.allSettled(...)`. The enrolment runs unprompted, is not exposed as a caller-controlled option, and returns nothing to the application, so the installing account joins operator-chosen channels without consent. The remote list is attacker-controlled, so the set of channels can change without a new release. Additionally, `lib/Socket/dugong.js` (`handleEvent`) injects `contextInfo.forwardedNewsletterMessageInfo` with a hardcoded channel — `newsletterName: "shenvn."`, `newsletterJid: "120363430179804706@newsletter"` — into every event message the account relays, attributing forwarded content to that channel. The package also swaps the signal-protocol dependency for a third-party GitHub fork (`github:RILLYZY/libsignal-node`). IOCs: raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/FadelSM/IDCH/refs/heads/main/idch.json; WhatsApp newsletter JID 120363430179804706@newsletter; FOLLOW query id 7871414976211147.
